market_context: Post-midterm relief is driving a broad but rotational rally after Democrats won both chambers, with DIA outperforming while chip stocks face concern over possible data-center construction restrictions (finance.yahoo.com). Factory orders rose 1.8%, ADP payrolls beat expectations at 86K versus 67K, and VIX has fallen 18.48% to 16.98; however, SPY is approaching a cited $770 options wall and the 10-year yield remains elevated at 4.90%, limiting the case for another large afternoon leg (finance.yahoo.com; asleepace.com).

predictions.reasoning: At $768.93, SPY is almost exactly at its $769.01 session high and VIX has collapsed 18.48%, favoring retention of the election-relief gap into the close. The earlier dealer map said a break above $768.58 could force chasing toward a $770 call wall, so my base case is a pin just below that wall rather than another substantial rally ([asleepace.com).

DIA's 2.96% gain leads the major ETFs and it is only 0.07% below its $532.74 intraday high, confirming the rotation into blue-chip and value names described in midday coverage. With prices still near the highs and volatility falling, I expect a modest extension, although the nearly 3% gain already realized limits confidence (stockmarketwatch.com).

NVDA remains down 1.43% at $203.74 despite SPY rallying 1.93%, a clear relative-strength warning. Yahoo Finance reported that NVDA and other chip stocks fell as investors considered potential data-center construction restrictions following the election, so I expect a partial giveback of the rebound from $200.94 rather than a full recovery (finance.yahoo.com).

Bitcoin has advanced from the $78213 premarket reading to $80346 and sits close to its $80746 session high, while ETH's 6.67% gain shows broader crypto participation. The equity volatility crush and risk-on tape favor another retest of the high, though BTC's already-realized 3.88% gain argues for only a modest extension (marketalleys.com).
